<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תשרי_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518914091_theRebbe_428" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_A9_D7_A8_D7_99_meluket__BH_POST_1766518914091_theRebbe_428__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section provides the header information for the maamar, including the Torah portion and date.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="1">Shabbat of Haazinu,</t>
    <t s="2">Shabbat Shuvah, 5740*</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section introduces the verse "Return O Israel until Hashem your G-d" and questions the specific wording and the use of the two Divine names.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"Return O Israel until Hashem your G-d"<sup>1</sup>,</t>
    <t s="1">And it is known regarding this the precise point of our Nesi'im: what is the meaning of saying "until Hashem your G-d," for seemingly it should have said "to Hashem your G-d"<sup>2</sup>.</t>
    <t s="2">And also the fact that it uses the two names Havayah and Elokecha<sup>3</sup>.</t>
    <t s="3">And especially since it says here "Return O Israel,"</t>
    <t s="4">for the name Israel describes the highest level within Israel,</t>
    <t s="5">for the Children of Israel are generally divided into two levels: Yaakov and Israel,</t>
    <t s="6">and the name Israel is because "you have striven with G-d and with men and have prevailed"<sup>4</sup>,</t>
    <t s="7">from which it is understood that it speaks here about the matter of the completeness of teshuvah<sup>5</sup>.</t>
    <t s="8">And as is also understood from the fact that the haftarah of Shabbat Teshuvah is "Shuvah Yisrael,"</t>
    <t s="9">that the teshuvah of Shabbat Teshuvah is a lofty level of teshuvah ila'ah.</t>
    <t s="10">For behold, Shabbat, the letters of which spell "tashev" (you shall return), is the aspect of teshuvah ila'ah<sup>6</sup>,</t>
    <t s="11">And within teshuvah ila'ah itself</t>
    <t s="12">[which has several levels]</t>
    <t s="13">it is a lofty teshuvah, for one must be all his days</t>
    <t s="14">(even on weekdays)</t>
    <t s="15">in teshuvah ila'ah<sup>7</sup>,</t>
    <t s="16">from which it is understood,</t>
    <t s="17">that Shabbat is a lofty level within teshuvah ila'ah itself.</t>
    <t s="18">And especially on Shabbat Teshuvah, which rectifies and elevates all the Shabbats of the year</t>
    <t s="19">[as explained in the writings of the Arizal<sup>8</sup></t>
    <t s="20">regarding the seven days between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur, which contain all seven days of the week,</t>
    <t s="21">that on the first day of the week within these days, they rectify and elevate all the Sundays of the entire year,</t>
    <t s="22">and likewise on the second day, etc.,</t>
    <t s="23">and on Shabbat Teshuvah they rectify and elevate all the Shabbats of the entire year],</t>
    <t s="24">for the teshuvah of Shabbat Teshuvah is loftier even than the teshuvah of all the Shabbats of the year,</t>
    <t s="25">and this teshuvah is analogous to Yom Kippur<sup>9</sup></t>
    <t s="26">about which it is written<sup>10</sup></t>
    <t s="27">"For on this day He shall atone for you... before Hashem you shall be purified,"</t>
    <t s="28">"before Hashem" specifically, above the name Havayah<sup>11</sup>,</t>
    <t s="29">and even more than this it says "He shall atone for you" simply, referring to the One who has no known name and is not grasped by any name, etc.<sup>12</sup>,</t>
    <t s="30">So why does it say here "until Hashem your G-d"?</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that "Return until Hashem your G-d" refers to the unification of Havayah and Elokim, a higher knowledge achieved through teshuvah, as opposed to the service of tzaddikim.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">2)</t>
    <t s="1">And the explanation of this is known<sup>13</sup>,</t>
    <t s="2">that what is written "Return O Israel until Hashem your G-d" is the matter of the unification of Havayah and Elokim, as it is written<sup>14</sup></t>
    <t s="3">"And you shall know... that Havayah, He is Elokim,"</t>
    <t s="4">which is a most lofty knowledge,</t>
    <t s="5">as explained in the Zohar<sup>15</sup>.</t>
    <t s="6">And therefore it says "Return O Israel until Hashem your G-d," because the matter of teshuvah is connected to this knowledge, as it is written<sup>16</sup></t>
    <t s="7">(regarding the matter of teshuvah that was on Mount Carmel)</t>
    <t s="8">"And they said, 'Hashem, He is Elokim; Hashem, He is Elokim.'"</t>
    <t s="9">And the repetition of "Hashem, He is Elokim; Hashem, He is Elokim" twice is because through the service of teshuvah,</t>
    <t s="10">which is above the service of tzaddikim,</t>
    <t s="11">the matter of "Hashem, He is Elokim" is drawn down twice.</t>
    <t s="12">And as it is brought in the Midrash<sup>17</sup></t>
    <t s="13">"At Sinai it was said<sup>18</sup></t>
    <t s="14">'I am Hashem your G-d'; at Carmel it was said doubly, 'Hashem, He is Elokim; Hashem, He is Elokim,'"</t>
    <t s="15">And it is explained in Likkutei Torah<sup>19</sup></t>
    <t s="16">that at Sinai, Israel was on the level of tzaddikim,</t>
    <t s="17">and through the service of tzaddikim</t>
    <t s="18">(the performance of mitzvos)</t>
    <t s="19">the matter of "Hashem, He is Elokim" was drawn down once,</t>
    <t s="20">but at Mount Carmel, through teshuvah, they drew down "Hashem, He is Elokim" twice.</t>
    <t s="21">And this is similar to what at the Giving of the Torah is written "I am Hashem your G-d,"</t>
    <t s="22">"I am" once,</t>
    <t s="23">but regarding teshuvah it is written<sup>20</sup></t>
    <t s="24">"I, I am He... for My sake...,"</t>
    <t s="25">"I" twice,</t>
    <t s="26">because through the service of performing mitzvos, the aspect of "I" is drawn down once,</t>
    <t s="27">but the drawing down through the service of teshuvah is higher than the drawing down through the service of performing mitzvos<sup>21</sup>.</t>
    <t s="28">For this is also the meaning of "I, I am He... for My sake," and Targum renders it "for the sake of My name,"</t>
    <t s="29">up to the aspect of His great name<sup>22</sup>,</t>
    <t s="30">and higher still, the aspect of "He and His name alone,"</t>
    <t s="31">before the tzimtzum.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
